plan: With a private value of $6, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the value is relatively low, I want to bid strategically. I'll consider that other bidders might use similar reasoning. A bid slightly above my value but not too high could work - perhaps around $7-$8. This gives me a chance to win if others bid conservatively, while limiting potential losses. I'll aim to bid just enough to have a reasonable chance of winning without overpaying.

My private value is $40. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This prevents underbidding (and potentially losing a profitable item) or overbidding (and potentially losing money). Since values are independently drawn, I can't predict other bidders' values. Bidding $40 ensures I win if my value is highest, and I only pay the second-highest bid. This maximizes my expected profit given the uncertainty.

With a private value of $28, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since values are drawn randomly and independently, I'll use a strategic bidding approach. I want to bid high enough to have a good chance of winning, but not so high that I risk losing money. A bid around my value makes sense - slightly above $28 to increase winning probability, but not dramatically over my true value to protect against potential losses.
